speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and dysuria. To begin my assessment, have you noticed any fever or chills accompanying these symptoms? Also, have you been able to pass urine today?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) secondary to Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection.

I have formed this diagnosis based on your age, sexually active status, dysuria, and specifically the history of dyspareunia (pain during intercourse) alongside severe lower abdominal pain. I will now request your test results to confirm the specific pathogen and any signs of tubo-ovarian abscess.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Gram Stain, and Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (NAAT) for Chlamydia and Gonorrhea.
REQUEST TEST: Pelvic Ultrasound.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound
